title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. College Friday night review: all five games of Friday, Nov. 6, graded, including the late finishes, New Mexico at Nevada and TCU at Arizona.

paragraphs: Friday put five college games on the board, and all five are final and graded here. The one that will keep South Florida backers up at night ended on a 55-yard field goal as time ran out in Greenville. It turned South Florida +1.5 from a cash into a loss on the last snap and left the Over 39.5 stuck at 37. SMU −5.5 and the Over 56.5 cruised, and Illinois +4.5 and the Under 52.5 never needed a sweat in Champaign. Late in Tucson, Arizona needed a muffed kickoff and a field goal with 38 seconds left just to win by one, and Arizona −6.5 lost anyway. In Reno, New Mexico won by 28, and Nevada +10.5 was never close.

Every game below is graded against the line printed on the card at kickoff, using ESPN finals and play-by-play, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Virginia Tech at SMU sat at SMU −6.5 with a total of 56.5 Friday morning and moved to SMU −5.5 in the evening refresh, with the Cover Writer on SMU and the Over all day, projecting SMU 32, Virginia Tech 25. South Florida at East Carolina moved from South Florida +2.5 to +1.5 with the total at 39.5, and the Cover Writer stayed on South Florida and the Over, projecting South Florida 23, East Carolina 22. Nebraska at Illinois stayed Illinois +4.5, and when the total climbed from 50.5 to 52.5 the Cover Writer flipped from the Over to the Under, projecting Nebraska 27, Illinois 23. New Mexico at Nevada kicked at New Mexico −10.5 with a total of 38.5, and the Cover Writer had Nevada +10.5 and the Over, projecting New Mexico 28, Nevada 18. TCU at Arizona kicked at Arizona −6.5 with a total of 46.5, and the Cover Writer had Arizona −6.5 and the Under, projecting Arizona 26, TCU 16. The kickoff numbers are what's graded here. South Florida +2.5 would have lost by half a point, and the Over 50.5 in Champaign would have lost by 13.5.

Follow The Money had a side only in Tucson, on TCU +6.5, and took the Over at SMU, in Champaign and in Tucson. In The Trenches had a side only in Tucson, on Arizona −6.5, and made no total picks. Letdown Watch made no picks Friday. Games without a pick aren't graded for them.

Card line: East Carolina −1.5, total 39.5. The Cover Writer's card had South Florida +1.5 and the Over, projecting South Florida 23, East Carolina 22. Final: South Florida 17, East Carolina 20. East Carolina won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

South Florida +1.5 was the kind of ticket you could hold with a straight face for 59 minutes and 58 seconds. Kromenhoek hit Rodgers for a 26-yard touchdown on the opening drive, Perez answered with a 44-yard field goal, Gramatica made it 10-3 from 30, and Williams found Sides from 15 yards out with 31 seconds left in the half. It was 10-10 at the break. South Florida +1.5 was covering by 1.5, and the total sat at 20, with the Over 39.5 needing 19.5 more.

The third quarter is where both tickets began to sweat. South Florida turned it over on downs at the East Carolina 32, and Williams hit Sides again from 8 yards out for a 17-10 East Carolina lead. Collins Jr. punched it in from a yard out at 9:42 of the fourth, it was 17-17, and South Florida +1.5 was right back to covering by 1.5. The total sat at 34. The Over 39.5 needed a touchdown, because a field goal would still leave it 2.5 short.

Then came nine and a half minutes of punts, sacks and flags. A South Florida holding call wiped out a breakup and handed East Carolina a fresh set of downs, and East Carolina punted anyway. South Florida punted it right back with under two minutes left and the game tied. On the last drive, an interference flag on South Florida moved East Carolina 10 yards to its own 49, Williams hit Gray for 18 to the South Florida 40, spiked it, and found Gray for 3 more to the 37. South Florida called timeout with two seconds left, and Andrew Conrad drilled a 55-yard field goal as time ran out. East Carolina 20, South Florida 17. South Florida +1.5 lost by 1.5 on the final snap, and the morning number of +2.5 would have lost by half a point. The Over needed a touchdown from somebody, got a field goal, and died at 37.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on South Florida +1.5, missed by 1.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 39.5, fell 2.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

items.matchup: College Friday · No sweat against the number

paragraphs: Card line: SMU −5.5, total 56.5. The Cover Writer's card had SMU −5.5 and the Over, projecting SMU 32, Virginia Tech 25. Final: Virginia Tech 28, SMU 51. SMU won by 23, and the teams scored 79 points.

SMU −5.5 never sweated, and the Over 56.5 got home with nine minutes to spare. Green ran 12 yards for a touchdown on the opening drive, Baird hit from 47, and Grunkemeyer snuck one in for Virginia Tech. Then came the turnover that tilted it. Grunkemeyer got sacked and stripped by White at the Virginia Tech 46, and Jennings hit Knight for a 46-yard touchdown on the very next snap. Overton ran 22 yards for a Virginia Tech touchdown, Baird made a 50-yarder with three seconds left in the half, and SMU led 23-14 at the break. SMU −5.5 was covering by 3.5, and the total sat at 37, 19.5 short of the Over.

Raphael ran in from 3 yards out, Virginia Tech turned it over on downs at the SMU 25, and Knight caught a 13-yard touchdown. It was 37-14 after three, SMU −5.5 was covering by 17.5, and the Over needed 5.5 more with a full quarter to play.

Knight's third touchdown, a 5-yarder from Jennings at 9:15 of the fourth, made it 44-14 and 58 points, and every Under 56.5 ticket in the building was torn up right there. Virginia Tech piled on backdoor points anyway, Overton from 2 with a two-point conversion and Grunkemeyer to Brown from 3, but Jennings answered with a 50-yard strike to Cooper and the SMU side never felt a breeze. SMU −5.5 covered by 17.5, and the Over cleared by 22.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on SMU −5.5, covered by 17.5 points. The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Over 56.5, cleared it by 22.5 points.
Missed: The Formula on the Under 56.5, went over by 22.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: Nebraska −4.5, total 52.5. The Cover Writer's card had Illinois +4.5 and the Under, projecting Nebraska 27, Illinois 23. Final: Nebraska 13, Illinois 24. Illinois won by 11, and the teams scored 37 points.

Illinois +4.5 and the Under 52.5 were cashing from the first quarter on, and Nebraska's kicker made sure of it. Hohl missed from 45 and again from 54 just before the half. In between, Nelson ran 15 yards for a Nebraska touchdown and Houser found Dixon from 3, and it was 7-7 at the break. Illinois +4.5 was covering by 4.5, and the total sat at 14, a mile under 52.5.

Houser hit Anderson from 5 yards out, Nebraska turned it over on downs late in the third, and Houser found Dixon again from 6 early in the fourth. It was 21-7 Illinois, and the Illinois ticket was covering by 18.5.

Colandrea hit Barney for a 51-yard touchdown, and the two-point try failed. Moczulski answered with a 21-yard field goal, 24-13. Nebraska turned it over on downs at 2:17 and again in the last minute, and that was it. Illinois +4.5 covered by 15.5, the Under stayed under by 15.5, and Nebraska −4.5 backers can send their complaints to the two missed kicks.
Called it: The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on Illinois +4.5, covered by 15.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Under 52.5, stayed under by 15.5 points.
Missed: The Formula on Nebraska −4.5, missed by 15.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 52.5, fell 15.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: New Mexico −10.5, total 38.5. The Cover Writer's card had Nevada +10.5 and the Over, projecting New Mexico 28, Nevada 18. Final: New Mexico 31, Nevada 3. New Mexico won by 28, and the teams scored 34 points.

Nevada +10.5 and the Over 38.5 were in trouble from the first quarter. Humphrey scored from 2 yards out, Sibley ran 31 yards for a touchdown, and New Mexico led 14-3 at the half after Fernandez's 32-yard field goal. Humphrey's second touchdown and Fa'avae's 25-yard throw to Keith made it 28-3, and Romero's 37-yard field goal capped it. New Mexico 31, Nevada 3. Nevada +10.5 lost by 17.5, and the Over 38.5 fell 4.5 points short with Nevada scoring a single field goal.
Called it: Next Man Up on New Mexico −10.5, covered by 17.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and The Formula on Nevada +10.5, missed by 17.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 38.5, fell 4.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: Arizona −6.5, total 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had Arizona −6.5 and the Under, projecting Arizona 26, TCU 16. Final: TCU 28, Arizona 29. Arizona won by 1, and the teams scored 57 points.

Arizona −6.5 looked like the right ticket for a quarter. Fifita hit Mizell for a 20-yard touchdown, Salgado-Medina added a 43-yard field goal, and Arizona led 10-0. Then Jaden Craig ran 7 yards for a TCU touchdown, and Hooper returned an interception 93 yards for another. TCU took a 14-10 lead into the half, Arizona −6.5 was losing by 10.5, and the total sat at 24, with the Under 46.5 holding 22.5 points of room.

Fifita ran in from 9 yards out, and Dwyer caught a 6-yard touchdown from Jaden Craig, so it was 21-17 TCU after three. Salgado-Medina's 23-yard field goal early in the fourth made it 21-20. Then Jaden Craig ran in from 2 yards out with 6:35 left, TCU led 28-20, and the total hit 48. The Under 46.5 was gone with six and a half minutes to play.

Arizona still needed a touchdown and a field goal just to win, and more than that to cover. Arizona's Quincy Craig fumbled at the TCU 9, and Fifita recovered at the 15. Fifita found Quincy Craig for a 15-yard touchdown with 1:45 left, and the two-point throw failed. TCU's Ed Small muffed a 35-yard kickoff, and Arizona's Zuri Watson recovered at the TCU 26. Salgado-Medina hit a 37-yard field goal with 38 seconds left, and Boss intercepted Jaden Craig on TCU's last drive. Arizona 29, TCU 28. Arizona −6.5 won the game and lost the ticket by 5.5, and the Under 46.5 went over by 10.5.
Called it: Follow The Money on TCU +6.5, covered by 5.5 points. Follow The Money on the Over 46.5, cleared it by 10.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Arizona −6.5, missed by 5.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Under 46.5, went over by 10.5 points.
No pick: In The Trenches on the total.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 2-3 against the spread and 2-3 on totals Friday, and that makes the week 5-7 on both. SMU −5.5 and Illinois +4.5 both cashed by double digits, and the Over at SMU and the Under in Champaign both cleared by more than two touchdowns. The late flip to the Under 52.5 looks a whole lot smarter today than the Over 50.5 would have. South Florida +1.5 was a winner until a 55-yard kick with no time on the clock, and the Over 39.5 died needing a touchdown and getting a field goal. Then the late games took two more of each. Nevada +10.5 lost by 17.5, and Arizona −6.5 won the game and still lost by 5.5. A walk-off in Greenville and a muffed kickoff in Tucson turned a good Friday into a losing one.

The Formula went 1-4 against the spread and 1-4 on totals Friday, 4-8 and 3-9 for the week. SMU −5.5 hit and the Under 52.5 in Champaign hit, and that's where the good news ends. Nebraska −4.5 lost by 15.5 while its kicker missed twice, the Under 56.5 at SMU was buried by the middle of the fourth, and South Florida took the same walk-off punch everybody else took. Nevada +10.5 and the Over in Reno both lost, and so did Arizona −6.5 and the Under in Tucson. Nine total losses in one week is a number The Formula would like scrubbed from the record.

Next Man Up went 3-2 against the spread and 2-3 on totals Friday, 7-5 and 6-6 for the week. It matched the Cover Writer ticket for ticket through the first three games, then split from it in Reno, where New Mexico −10.5 covered by 17.5. Arizona −6.5 and the Under in Tucson burned it the same as everybody else. For the week, Next Man Up is two games ahead of the Cover Writer on sides and one ahead on totals.

Follow The Money went 1-0 against the spread and 2-1 on totals Friday, 3-1 and 4-3 for the week. The money liked the Over at SMU and got paid, then liked the Over in Champaign and watched Nebraska miss two field goals. Even the market can't buy a kick. It closed the night by cashing TCU +6.5 and the Over in Tucson.
In The Trenches went 0-1 against the spread and made no total picks Friday, 4-1 for the week. The perfect week died late in Tucson with Arizona −6.5.
Letdown Watch made no picks Friday, and it hasn't made one all week.
